summary: ansible-test is the main collection testing tool; run it from the collection root inside an ansible_collections path, target the ansible-core versions you support, and use Docker to avoid installing requirements. CI is typically Azure Pipelines or GitHub Actions via collection_template.
questions: Where do I need to run ansible-test from when testing a collection?
Why does ansible-test say my collection isn't in an ansible_collections directory?
Can I run collection tests without installing all the dependencies locally?
What CI do big community collections use for tests?

answer_card.title: Testing tools for collections
answer_card.answer_md:
- Use `ansible-test` (in both `ansible` and `ansible-core`).
- Run it **from the collection root**, which must sit under an `ansible_collections` path, e.g. `collections/ansible_collections/community/general`.
- Test against the ansible-core versions you target.
- Use `--docker` to run in containers without extra local requirements.
- Large collections use Azure Pipelines; many others use GitHub Actions with the `collection_template` workflows.
